title: Tensor flatness and relative stalk flatness on one pulled-back affine chart
statement: Let $A,T$ be commutative rings, $X,Y$ schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} A$, and $M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $U$ be one affine open of $X$, with no covering hypothesis. Let $q:A\to T$, $p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec} A$, and $e:Y\simeq\operatorname{Spec} T$ satisfy $\operatorname{Spec}(q)\circ e=p$. Give $N=\Gamma(M,U)$ its $A$-module action through the map $A\to\Gamma(X,U)$ induced by $f$ and the canonical spectrum-sections isomorphism. Put $Z=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec} A}Y$ and $G=\operatorname{tensorPullback}(\operatorname{pr}_X)(M)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $T\otimes_A N$ is flat over $T$ if and only if, for every $z\in Z$ with $\operatorname{pr}_X(z)\in U$, the module stalk $G_z$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], restricted along the stalk map of $\operatorname{pr}_Y$, is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,\operatorname{pr}_Y(z)}$. No flatness condition is imposed outside this inverse-image chart.

proof.text: Put B=Gamma(X,U), N=Gamma(M,U), and W=(pullback.fst f p) inverse U. The affine-spectrum fibre-product formula identifies W over Y, using e and he, with Spec(B tensor_A T). Its section ring C is B tensor_A T with the structural map from T given by the second projection. The affine pullback section comparison identifies Gamma(tensorPullback M,W) with N tensor_B C, compatibly with C-scalar multiplication.

Swap tensor factors and reassociate: C tensor_B N = (B tensor_A T) tensor_B N is T-linearly isomorphic to T tensor_A N. The maps on pure tensors send (b tensor t) tensor n to t tensor (b*n), with inverse t tensor n sent to (1 tensor t) tensor n. Balancing verifies both inverse equations and the T-action. These are isomorphisms of actual section modules, not arbitrary chosen witnesses.

The tensor pullback is quasi-coherent because it is the uniquely determined left adjoint to pushforward, hence isomorphic to Mathlib module pullback. At each point z of W, the affine stalk tensor presentation identifies the localization of the chart section module at its prime with the actual pullback stalk. Germ-stalkMap compatibility identifies the restriction of the T-action with the second projection stalk map. The isomorphism e identifies the base stalk with T localized at the inverse-image prime, compatibly with the section maps; he supplies the structural equation.

Apply the relative local criterion of 00HT (6), equivalently Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization followed by Module.flat_of_isLocalized_maximal: the section module on Spec C is T-flat exactly when each of these stalk modules is flat over the corresponding localized base ring. Transfer through the section and base-stalk equivalences. W is exactly the set of points z with fst(z) in U, giving the stated equivalence. Empty U and zero T give zero sections and no points; the zero module also satisfies both sides.

theorem affine_pullback_chart_tensor_flat_iff_stalks
    (A T : CommRingCat.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec A)
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] (U : X.affineOpens)
    (q : A ⟶ T) (p : Y ⟶ Spec A) (e : Y ≅ Spec T)
    (he : e.hom ≫ Spec.map q = p) :
    (letI : Module (A : Type u) Γ(M, U.1) :=
      Module.compHom _ (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv ≫
        f.appLE ⊤ U.1 (by simp)).hom)
     letI : Algebra (A : Type u) (T : Type u) := q.hom.toAlgebra
     Module.Flat (T : Type u) ((T : Type u) ⊗[(A : Type u)] Γ(M, U.1))) ↔
    (∀ z : ↥(pullback f p : Scheme.{u}), (pullback.fst f p) z ∈ U.1 →
      Module.Flat (Y.presheaf.stalk ((pullback.snd f p) z))
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((pullback.snd f p).stalkMap z).hom).obj
          ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor (pullback f p).toRingedSpace z).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.fst f p)).obj M))))
